analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING 1) CNH Update, 2) RBA Recap, 3) Dom Wilson's Latest, 4) US Midterms, 5) Raising Our NatGas Forecasts 3 Nov 2026
key_insights: PBoC raised the FX reserve requirement ratio by 2 points to push back against fast yuan appreciation. GS desks see limited liquidity impact (about $24bn removed from $1.2tn of onshore USD deposits) and treat it as a signal, not a line in the sand for spot.

China Macro Trading sees the spot-fixing gap, which widened from -300 to -700 pips in October and bounced to -430, as the timing guide. A narrowing to -300 or higher would be a good point to re-engage USDCNH shorts.

EM Strategy sees a 200-300 pip spot-fixing gap (6.68-6.69 USDCNY) as a good risk-reward area to fade. It expects a faster fixing appreciation before the APEC meeting in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19, and a 6.70-71 maximum on position unwind if US-Iran escalates.

Asia Econ says CNY has strengthened at a 9.5% annualised pace against the USD since end-September, which is likely too much. It expects gradual appreciation to be managed rather than reversed and keeps its 12-month USDCNY forecast at 6.40.

The RBA raised the cash rate 25bp to 4.85% in a 6-3 vote, in line with GS and consensus. GS views it as incrementally dovish because of the split vote, the dropped tightening-bias language and a trimmed mean inflation forecast of 2.4% by 4Q2028.
Governor Bullock said there are now five rate increases in the system and that it is a good point to take stock and watch the data. The bill curve re-flattened after the statement.
GS Aus IRP sales prefers paying 3m3m and sees risk building further out the curve (1y1y and beyond) for rate cuts to get priced. It sees 3m3m 1y1y flatteners as supported from here.

GS Global Macro says forward real rates moved above their prior range in July 2026 after the energy shock and AI capex upgrades, as the Fed signalled and delivered hikes. The funds rate has troughed above 3.6%.
GS argues the 5.3% peak of the last hiking cycle likely anchors deep forward rates. With a modal Fed funds peak of 4-4.25%, forward rates above 5% look less plausible.

On the US midterms, GS FX Strategy sees little policy difference between a blue sweep and a split Congress for Iran and AI regulation, since the President can use executive action. A blue sweep may mean incrementally higher spending, and the USD effect is unclear.

Democrats may focus on cutting tariffs on Canadian imports, which could be positive for CAD in the medium term. Democratic wins in key states would likely bring more state-level data center restrictions.

GS Commodities raised its 1Q27 TTF forecast to 74 EUR/MWh from 44 and its 2027 average to 51 from 32. The change reflects a 45% subjective probability of a low-winter Mideast LNG supply scenario (worth 26 EUR) and a cold-weather component (worth 4 EUR).

Risks to the TTF forecast skew up. A low-supply scenario plus a 1 std. deviation colder winter would lift 1Q27 TTF to nearly 150 EUR/MWh. The current 1Q27 price of 92 EUR/MWh implies a 47% market-perceived probability of that scenario.

risk_factors: The CNH funding could loosen enough to change the carry profile, which would affect the USDCNH short.
US-Iran escalation could push USDCNY to 6.70-71 on position unwind.
The polling error in the US midterms may only be clear over days or weeks, especially for the Senate.
Inflation expectations in Australia carry upside risk, per Governor Bullock.
TTF risks skew to the upside from a low-winter Mideast LNG supply scenario and a colder NW European winter.
Market pricing of forward rates above 5% would be unusual unless the market expects the Fed to hike above the prior peak.
charts_described: Chart 1 in the RBA section lists the RBA run: cash rate 4.855 mid, 9-Dec-26 at 4.890, 10-Feb-27 at 4.948, 24-Mar-27 at 4.955, 5-May-27 at 4.960, 23-Jun-27 at 4.920, and 1y1y at 4.740.
vol_and_positioning: In RBA positioning, hedge funds had been paying the first three meetings and receiving further out the curve. After the statement HFs paid the dip in Dec and Feb RBA, and bills re-flattened, unwinding much of their recent steepening.
Term premium paying in 1y1y and 2y1y came from those who had received into the morning steepening, which was +5bp at one point.
The CNH DF curve lowered only modestly after the PBoC move. Offshore/onshore basis widened from around par to -40 in October and recovered to within -10.
geopolitical: Possible US-Iran escalation could push USDCNY to 6.70-71 on position unwind, per EM Strategy.
Trump is expected at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19.
Iran policy is one of the biggest open questions from the US midterms, but GS sees limited difference between a blue sweep and a split Congress.
A low-winter Mideast LNG supply scenario is built into the TTF forecast, with Qatari LNG exports assumed to reach operational max in Feb27.
Democrats may focus on reducing tariffs on imports from Canada.

tension_points.bull_case: Trade balance supports about 6% annualised CNH appreciation since mid-2025, and GS keeps a 12-month USDCNY forecast of 6.40.
tension_points.bear_case: The 9.5% annualised pace since end-September is likely too much, and the PBoC is pushing back through the RRR hike and daily fixings.
tension_points.what_invalidates: CNH funding loosening enough to change the carry profile, or a spot-fixing gap narrowing to -300 or higher, which would be the signal to re-engage USDCNH shorts.

tension_points.bull_case: Capacity pressures are greater than judged before and inflation expectations carry upside risk, so further hikes remain possible.
tension_points.bear_case: The split vote, dropped tightening-bias language and a trimmed mean forecast below the mid-point point to a pause after five increases.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A data surprise that raises inflation expectations, since Bullock said the Board will watch incoming data.
